Case: Patient D is a 66-year-old Black man with history of hepatocellular carcinoma who presents with acute mid back pain. Patient D states that the pain started after he attempted lifting a heavy piece of furniture yesterday. Patient D also endorses that the pain is even more severe when he attempts to bend or stretch his back. When you examine Patient D, you notice that he is tender to palpation in the mid-thoracic spine, and that he has a positive Romberg sign. You obtain MRI of the thoracic spine, which reveals diffuse osseous metastatic lesions with a severe pathologic fracture at T6.
